To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: [Insert date]
Subject: Aligning transportation cost and carbon impact under practical operating rules

Context
Our network ships finished goods from multiple warehouses to multiple retail stores. Every lane has two performance measures: a per‑unit variable spend and a per‑unit carbon impact. In many cases, the lowest‑cost lanes are also more carbon‑intensive. We need a plan that reflects our financial discipline and our sustainability commitments without compromising store service.

Operational realities we must honor
- Route activation costs: Starting to ship on any lane triggers a one‑time setup charge (e.g., contracts, customs, dock preparation). This charge applies whenever the lane is active, regardless of volume.
- Minimum order quantities: Activated lanes must move at least a defined threshold to justify equipment utilization; partial loads are not accepted on these lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: To stay within receiving dock capacity and keep vendor management manageable, each store may be served by only a limited number of warehouses.

Supply and demand boundaries
- Warehouses have finite inventory available for dispatch; shipments cannot exceed local supply.
- Each store has a minimum demand that must be covered reliably within the planning period.

Management priorities and evaluation approach
Leadership has set the relative importance of cost and emissions. We will score any feasible shipping plan using a blended total that:
- Applies the cost importance to total variable shipping spend,
- Applies the emissions importance to total carbon emitted,
- Adds all route setup/activation charges at full value (these are not discounted or weighted).
The plan with the lowest blended total, while meeting service and operational requirements, will be selected.

Business goal
Identify which lanes to activate and determine shipment quantities on each active lane so that:
- Warehouse inventories are not exceeded,
- All store demand requirements are met,
- Any activated lane moves at least its minimum order quantity,
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of suppliers,
- The resulting blended total (weighted variable cost plus weighted emissions, plus full setup charges) is as low as possible under the rules above.
We will provide a clear recommendation that lists activated lanes, planned volumes, expected spend, and expected emissions, along with key trade‑offs for leadership review.
